title: Patch Néron models across a finite complement on a Dedekind base
statement: Let $D$ be a Dedekind domain, $E=\operatorname{Frac}(D)$ and $S=\operatorname{Spec}D$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Let $V$ be a smooth separated finite-type $E$-scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Suppose $U\subseteq S$ is a nonempty open with finite complement consisting of closed points $s_1,\ldots,s_r$. Suppose there is a smooth separated finite-type $U$-scheme $M_U$ with $(M_U)_E\simeq V$ satisfying the mapping property for every smooth $U$-scheme. For every $i$ put $T_i=\operatorname{Spec}D_{s_i}$ and suppose there is a smooth separated finite-type $T_i$-scheme $M_i$ with $(M_i)_E\simeq V$ satisfying the mapping property for every smooth $T_i$-scheme. Then there are a smooth separated finite-type $S$-scheme $M$ and a generic isomorphism $M_E\simeq V$ satisfying the mapping property for every smooth $S$-scheme. Moreover $M\times_SU\simeq M_U$ and $M\times_ST_i\simeq M_i$ by isomorphisms respecting the given generic identifications. For a base $W$ equal to $U$, $T_i$ or $S$, the mapping property for a $W$-scheme $M$ equipped with $M_E\simeq V$ means that restriction followed by this isomorphism is a bijection $\operatorname{Hom}_W(X,M)\to\operatorname{Hom}_E(X_E,V)$ for every smooth $W$-scheme $X$, where $X_E=X\times_W\operatorname{Spec}E$ [def-pc-base-change, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Here a Dedekind domain means a Noetherian integrally closed domain of Krull dimension one. A group scheme over a scheme $T$ consists of multiplication, inverse and identity $T$-morphisms satisfying the group diagrams; it is commutative if multiplication is invariant under interchange of the two factors. Separated means that the diagonal is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion].

source.place: BLR 1.4 Proposition 1, implication (b) to (a), and its proof (printed p.18, PDF p.24), using 1.2 Lemma 5 and Proposition 4; patching input of 1.4 Theorem 3; primary-source scan read at https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/~kamenova/homepage_files/Bosch_Raynaud_Neron_Model_tc.pdf; project literature copy WANTED

proof.text: Write $\eta=\operatorname{Spec}E$. We use finite presentation in the sense locally of finite presentation, quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Each given model is finitely presented over its base: smoothness supplies local finite presentation; finite type supplies quasi-compactness; separatedness supplies quasi-separatedness (the implication is explicitly included in [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-over-affine], locally over affine base opens). The same applies to any affine smooth $S$-scheme $Z$: the map between affines $Z\to S$ is quasi-compact and separated, and is locally finitely presented by smoothness. Restrictions to affine base neighbourhoods are again finitely presented. For a point $s\in S$, use the directed system of affine open neighbourhoods of $s$, with reverse inclusion: [lem-weil-pbc-local-ring-spec-limit-affine-neighbourhoods] supplies its qcqs bases, affine transition maps, and limit $\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{S,s}$. We also use this at $\eta$, where $\mathcal O_{S,\eta}=E$. Thus all applications below of [thm-pd-spreading-out] have precisely its required kind of index system. No assertion that a stalk spectrum is an open subscheme is used.

source.place: Tags 01ZM (lemma-descend-finite-presentation) and 0GWT (lemma-morphism-glueing-near-closed-point), affine-neighbourhood limit in its proof

proof.text: For each $i$, apply clause (1) of [thm-pd-spreading-out] to $M_i\to T_i$ and the neighbourhood system of $s_i$. Obtain an affine neighbourhood $W_i$ of $s_i$, a finitely presented $W_i$-scheme $N_i$, and an isomorphism $(N_i)_{T_i}\simeq M_i$. The stage $N_i$ is qcqs: $N_i\to W_i$ is of finite presentation, so in particular quasi-compact and quasi-separated, and $W_i$ is affine, so [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-over-affine] applies. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-descend-smooth-qcqs] to $N_i\to W_i$; its stage map is locally finitely presented and its limit is the smooth $M_i$. Shrink $W_i$ to an affine neighbourhood where $N_i$ is smooth. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-descend-separated] to the same structural morphism and shrink again to make it separated. In both cases the source and target are qcqs, and shrinking preserves finite presentation. Remove the finitely many other $s_j$ and choose an affine neighbourhood of $s_i$ inside what remains. Now $W_i\cap(S\setminus U)=\{s_i\}$. Give $(N_i)_E$ its identification with $V$ induced from the specified one on $M_i$.

source.place: Tags 01ZM (lemma-descend-finite-presentation), 0C0C (lemma-descend-smooth), 01ZQ (lemma-descend-separated-finite-presentation); schemes.tex Tag 01K4 (lemma-quasi-compact-affine) for the qcqs stage

proof.text: Fix $i$ and choose an affine open $A_i\subseteq W_i\cap U$ containing $\eta$. Over $E$ there is the specified comparison $e_{i,E}:(N_i)_E\simeq(M_U)_E$, obtained through $V$. Apply clause (2) of [thm-pd-spreading-out], over the affine-neighbourhood system of $\eta$ inside $A_i$, to $e_{i,E}$ and its inverse. The restricted models are finitely presented by step 1. After taking a common smaller affine neighbourhood, both maps are defined. Their two composites become identities over $E$; clause (3) applied twice, followed by a common shrinking, makes them identities already on an affine open $G_i\subseteq A_i$. Thus we have an actual isomorphism $e_i:(N_i)_{G_i}\simeq(M_U)_{G_i}$ inducing exactly the specified generic comparison, rather than merely an unspecified isomorphism of the two generic fibres.

source.place: Tag 01ZM (lemma-descend-finite-presentation), clauses (2) and (3), applied to a map, its inverse, and the two inverse identities

proof.text: The closed subset $S\setminus G_i$ of $S$ contains no generic point. Every point in it is closed in $S$: a nonzero prime of the dimension-one domain $D$ is maximal. The scheme $S=\operatorname{Spec}D$ is Noetherian ($D$ is a Noetherian ring and $S$ is affine, hence quasi-compact), so [lem-sc-noetherian-closed-points-finite] makes $S\setminus G_i$ finite, and therefore its subset $W_i\setminus G_i$ is a finite set of closed points of $W_i$; any subset of it is closed in $W_i$. Delete from $W_i$ every point of this set except $s_i$, and call the resulting open $B_i$. Then $s_i\in B_i$, $B_i\subseteq W_i$, and $B_i\cap U=G_i$. Replace $N_i$ by its restriction to $B_i$. The isomorphism $e_i$ is now defined on the entire overlap with $U$. Also $T_i\to S$ factors through $B_i$: every open containing $s_i$ contains its generalizations, and the primes of $D_{s_i}$ contract to such primes of $D$. Thus the identification $(N_i)_{T_i}\simeq M_i$ is preserved. For $i\ne j$, $B_i\cap B_j\subseteq U$ because $B_i$ contains no missing point except $s_i$.

source.place: Noetherian closed-subset finiteness as stated in lem-sc-noetherian-closed-points-finite; elementary prime-chain argument for a dimension-one domain

proof.text: On the base cover $S=U\cup\bigcup_iB_i$, take the models $M_U$ and $N_i$. Glue $N_i$ to $M_U$ using $e_i$ on $B_i\cap U$. On $B_i\cap B_j$ the transition from $N_i$ to $N_j$ is $e_j^{-1}e_i$. Identity and cocycle conditions hold: on a triple intersection the product $(e_k^{-1}e_j)(e_j^{-1}e_i)$ equals $e_k^{-1}e_i$. All these intersections lie in $U$, so all indicated maps are defined on the whole required overlap. Apply [lem-galois-glue] to obtain an $S$-scheme $M$ with $M_U$ and the $N_i$ as these base restrictions. Consequently $M\times_SU\simeq M_U$ and $M\times_ST_i\simeq M_i$. The generic identifications agree through the $e_i$, giving one specified $M_E\simeq V$.

source.place: Tags 01JB (lemma-glue), 01JC (lemma-glue-schemes), relative gluing over the open cover of S

proof.text: The structural morphism $M\to S$ is separated by [lem-sfb-separated-lfp-target-open-locality], since its restrictions over $U$ and the $B_i$ are separated. It is smooth because each restriction is smooth: in the affine-local smooth-ring-map description of [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], every point has its required charts inside one of these base opens. Local finite type in the sense of [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]: let $Y=\operatorname{Spec}A'$ be an affine open of $S$ and $x\in M$ over $Y$. Choose $O\in\{U,B_1,\ldots,B_r\}$ containing the image of $x$. The restriction over $O$ is smooth, hence locally of finite presentation, so [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] gives affine opens $P=\operatorname{Spec}A\ni x$ of $M$ and $Q=\operatorname{Spec}R\subseteq O$ with $P$ mapping into $Q$ and $R\to A$ of finite presentation, in particular finitely generated. By [lem-sc-affine-inter-principal-both] there are $h\in R$ and $g\in A'$ with $D_Q(h)=D_Y(g)$ containing the image of $x$. Then the inverse image of $D_Q(h)$ in $P$ is $\operatorname{Spec}A_h$, an affine open containing $x$ inside the preimage of $Y$, and $A_h$ is finitely generated over $R_h=\mathcal O_S(D_Q(h))=A'_g$, hence over $A'$ (adjoin $1/g$). These opens cover the preimage of $Y$. Each restriction is quasi-compact: $M_U\to U$ is of finite type by hypothesis and $N_i\to B_i$ is of finite presentation; [lem-pc-quasi-compact-local-on-target] therefore gives quasi-compactness of $M\to S$. By [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] it is of finite type. This is gluing over an open cover of the BASE; arbitrary gluing of separated schemes along source opens would not establish separatedness.

source.place: Tag 01V8 (lemma-smooth-characterize), smoothness affine-locally; separatedness and quasi-compactness target-open locality as in the cited nodes

proof.text: First prove uniqueness for an affine smooth $S$-scheme $Z$. Suppose $a,b:Z\to M$ induce the same generic morphism to $V$. Over $U$ they coincide by the assumed mapping property of $M_U$, applied to the smooth $U$-scheme $Z_U$; smoothness after base change is [lem-pc-proper-base-change](2). Similarly their pullbacks to $T_i$ coincide by the mapping property of $M_i$, since $Z_{T_i}$ is smooth over $T_i$. Choose an affine neighbourhood $H_i\subseteq B_i$ of $s_i$. Both $Z_{H_i}$ and $M_{H_i}$ are finitely presented over $H_i$ (step 1). Clause (3) of [thm-pd-spreading-out], with limit $T_i$ as supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-local-ring-spec-limit-affine-neighbourhoods], makes $a$ and $b$ equal over some smaller neighbourhood $H'_i$ of $s_i$. The opens $U,H'_1,\ldots,H'_r$ cover $S$, hence their inverse images cover $Z$. The uniqueness assertion of [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-morphism-gluing] now gives $a=b$. This proves injectivity without any finite-type hypothesis on a general smooth test scheme.

source.place: Tag 01ZM (lemma-descend-finite-presentation), clause (3); schemes.tex Tags 01JB/01JC, uniqueness for open-cover gluing

proof.text: Now let $Z$ be affine smooth over $S$, and let $u_E:Z_E\to V$. The given mapping properties produce $u_U:Z_U\to M_U$ and $u_i:Z_{T_i}\to M_i$. Use the identifications of step 5. For each $i$ choose an affine $H_i\subseteq B_i$ containing $s_i$. Apply clause (2) of [thm-pd-spreading-out] to the map $u_i$, using the finitely presented $H_i$-schemes $Z_{H_i}$ and $M_{H_i}$ and the neighbourhood limit $T_i$. It yields a map $v_i:Z_{H'_i}\to M_{H'_i}$ for some affine neighbourhood $H'_i\subseteq H_i$ of $s_i$, whose restriction to $T_i$ is exactly $u_i$. Its generic restriction is therefore $u_E$. On $H'_i\cap U$, compare $v_i$ with $u_U$ as maps to $M_U$; their source is smooth over $U$ by [lem-pc-proper-base-change](2) and composition with the open inclusion (smoothness is local on affine charts in [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]). The mapping property of $M_U$ makes them equal. If $i\ne j$, $H'_i\cap H'_j\subseteq U$, so the same argument makes $v_i$ and $v_j$ equal there. Glue these maps to $Z\to M$ by [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-morphism-gluing]. Its generic restriction is $u_E$, proving surjectivity for affine smooth $Z$.

source.place: Tag 01ZM (lemma-descend-finite-presentation), clause (2); schemes.tex Tags 01JB/01JC, open-cover morphism gluing

proof.text: For an arbitrary smooth $S$-scheme $X$ and $u_E:X_E\to V$, cover $X$ by affine opens $Z_a$. Smoothness restricts to these opens by its affine-local description. Step 8 constructs a map $Z_a\to M$ extending $u_E|_{(Z_a)_E}$. On each affine open of $Z_a\cap Z_b$, step 7 makes the two maps equal; open-cover uniqueness then makes them equal on all of $Z_a\cap Z_b$. By [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-morphism-gluing] they glue to $X\to M$. Conversely, any two such maps agree on every affine open by step 7, so they agree on $X$. Thus restriction is bijective for every smooth test scheme, even one that is not quasi-compact or separated. Together with steps 5 and 6 this proves every assertion. If $r=0$, take $M=M_U$ since $U=S$; the argument uses no missing-point charts. Empty test schemes and an empty $V$ cause no exception: all uses are the given Hom bijections and finite-presentation descent, and empty schemes are allowed there.

source.place: Tags 01JB/01JC (lemma-glue and lemma-glue-schemes), morphism gluing and its uniqueness
